Name: PENABLE
Structural Path: PENABLE -> APB access qualification -> PADDIR/GPIOLOCK write enable -> gpio_dir
Attack Mechanisms: On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PENABLE` is one term of the three-way APB write qualification guarding the PADDIR case. A stuck-at or transient assertion of `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PENABLE` can turn a non-write or wrong-phase transfer into a PADDIR update. The supporting RTL chain is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PENABLE -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. The GPIO direction register accepts data on a cycle that should not perform a protected write.
Justification: A protocol-phase fault converts or suppresses the access cycle that updates the direction register.

Name: r_gpio_lock
Structural Path: r_gpio_lock -> PADDIR write authorization -> r_gpio_dir -> gpio_dir
Attack Mechanisms: `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock[0]` selects whether `PWDATA` or zero is assigned to `pwdata_l` in the PADDIR case. The relevant dataflow is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.pwdata_l -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. A fault that clears `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock[0]` admits an otherwise blocked direction write, while a fault that sets it during a legitimate write forces the captured direction word to zero. The lock policy no longer preserves the authorized pad-direction configuration.

A fault that sets `r_gpio_lock[0]` selects the `pwdata_l = '0` branch, yet the following nonblocking assignment to `r_gpio_dir` still executes. The relevant dataflow is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.pwdata_l -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. During a legitimate PADDIR write with `PSEL`, `PENABLE`, and `PWRITE` asserted, software expects an unlocked register to capture `PWDATA`. The injected lock-bit fault therefore replaces the requested direction bitmap with all zeros at the active `HCLK` edge. Every affected pad is forced toward input mode, corrupting the primary asset even though the bus transaction itself is legal.
Justification: A one-bit lock fault removes write protection and was highly feasible with essentially no masking.

Name: PWDATA
Structural Path: PWDATA -> write-data path -> r_gpio_dir update -> gpio_dir
Attack Mechanisms: `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA` carries the direction bitmap selected by the lock check immediately before `r_gpio_dir <= pwdata_l`. The relevant dataflow is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.pwdata_l -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. Flipping bits of `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA` in the admitted write cycle changes the bitmap captured by `r_gpio_dir`. Pins are configured as outputs or inputs contrary to the authorized software value.
Justification: A data-line fault directly corrupts the value captured into the direction state.

Name: PADDR
Structural Path: PADDR -> s_apb_addr -> register decode -> PADDIR write enable -> gpio_dir
Attack Mechanisms: On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR` supplies the address decode that distinguishes `REG_PADDIR` from the other GPIO registers. A transient address fault on `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR` during an APB write can redirect that write into `REG_PADDIR`. The supporting RTL chain is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. The presented `PWDATA` is captured into `r_gpio_dir`, changing pad directions without the intended direction-register access.
Justification: An address fault redirects a legal APB write into the direction-register decode.
